*Under the old patent law, the GCC Patent Law provided for a unitary right covering the above six-member state and a granted patent will automatically be valid in these countries. Until 6 January 2021, it was possible to obtain a national and regional patent for the same invention at the GCC Patent Office. The GCC Patent Office announced in its 20th session that it will stop accepting filing of patent applications with immediate effect. To obtain protection in the GCC, a separate application has to be filed in each of its member states. The GCC Patent Office recently announced that, as from 1 January 2023, will resume receiving new patent applications. The Head of Filing and Grant at the GCC Patent Office confirmed that only 12-month convention applications can be filed (as was the case in the past). Also, one application can cover both, Bahrain and Kuwait. At this stage, there is no indication of the estimated timeline for disclosing information regarding the services to be rendered by the GCC Patent Office on behalf Saudi Arabia, Oman, Qatar and UAE. The on-line system does not currently allow electing any of these countries when filing a GCC application. To obtain protection in Saudi Arabia, Oman, Qatar and UAE, we recommend separate applications to be filed in each of its member state.
Power of Attorney, notarised and legalised up to the Embassy/Consulate of any of the GCC member states
Deed of Assignment (if inventor and applicant differ), notarised and legalised up to the Embassy/Consulate of any of the GCC member states

The time period for filing formality documents at the GCC Patent Office is within three months from the latest of the filing date or issuance date of a formal examination report.
